subject: Cascadia RFP: BYOK/HSM integration details and test plan
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Initial BYOK/HSM integration questions + proposed test plan

Hi Fiona —

Thanks for including Redwood in the Cascadia RFP. To keep the BYOK portion of the security questionnaire moving, here's a short summary of the implementation options we support and a list of the items we'd need from you to validate integration during the procurement phase. Attached: BYOK-Integration-Diagram.pdf

What Redwood supports (short):
- Customer-managed keys: support for KMIP-backed HSMs and PKCS#11 where customers expose a KMIP proxy.
- Wrapped-key model: Redwood can accept customer-wrapped DEKs (AES-GCM key wrap) with short-lived unwrapping via a customer-provided HSM or a split-wrapping flow.
- Live attestation: optional remote attestation for supported HSMs (CloudHSM, Thales, Utimaco).
- TLS: mTLS (TLS 1.3) for HSM control channel; server authentication + client cert pinning supported.

Items we need from Cascadia to proceed:
1) HSM vendor and model (make/model + firmware) and FIPS 140-2/3 cert (PDF).
2) KMIP endpoint(s) (host:port), or PKCS#11 details if applicable; if behind a proxy, doc on proxy config.
3) HSM serial numbers for test units and an expected concurrency/ops/sec number for unwrap/wrap calls.
4) Preferred BYOK workflow: a) full-wrap + send DEKs, b) remote unwrapping via peered HSM, or c) split key (Redwood partial key + customer partial key).
5) Windows for an integration test (recommended 3 half-day windows).

Proposed Redwood test plan (high level):
- Day 0: exchange certs and validate TLS/mTLS handshake.
- Day 1: basic KMIP/PKCS#11 smoke tests, prove key creation/list/attributes.
- Day 2: wrap/unwrap performance and load verification, verify metadata (key usage, exportability).
- Day 3: rotation & fallback test (rotate DEK, ensure continued decrypt for existing tokens during alias window).

Could you confirm which BYOK workflow you prefer and send over the HSM certs/endpoint details to the Drive link? Once we have that, we can lock a test week and produce an HSM interop checklist.

Thanks —
Sooj

Fiona —

Appreciate the details. Quick technical clarifications from the runtime/ops side:
- We can support the wrapped-key flow where Cascadia performs the unwrap inside its HSM and returns wrapped DEKs to Redwood, or Redwood can be configured to call your KMIP endpoint to perform unwrapping via KMIP import/wrap-key semantics. For the latter we will need a routable endpoint and a secure channel (mTLS) with mutual auth.
- Our preferred cipher/transport: TLS 1.3 (RFC8446), AEAD cipher suites (TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 or TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384). We also support TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 with per-host cert pinning.
- For KMIP: we use client cert + basic KMIP username/password fallback; we prefer PKCS#11 only when you can provide a bridge/proxy that exposes a KMIP API.

Operational asks for the test window:
1) Provide routable KMIP host and a VPN or peered VPC path for Redwood test instances (we prefer a private VPC peering for throughput tests).
2) Confirm whether the HSM will accept our client certs signed by your CA or whether Cascadia will issue per-host client certs for Redwood test machines.
3) Share expected key attributes (algorithm, key length, usage flags) for the DEKs we will be exchanging.

One note on attestation: if Cascadia can provide the FIPS cert + module serial + vendor statement, that meets procurement in most cases. For production we recommend remote attestation; if Cascadia has a ReadyAttest or similar capability, we can add that as an option.

I'll draft a short HSM interop checklist and circulate (will attach to the thread).

Thanks,
Marcus
Principal Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

Fiona / team —

Attached is the draft HSM-interop-checklist.xlsx with the evidence and test vectors we will need for compliance review and procurement sign-off. High level items we will request during the integration window:
- FIPS 140-2/3 certificate (scanned PDF).
- HSM module serial numbers and firmware digest.
- Signed vendor attestation (PDF) that the modules are in the configuration claimed.
- Certificate chain for the KMIP endpoint (PEM bundle) and OCSP responder details.
- Test vectors: one wrapped DEK (AES-256) + expected plaintext to validate unwrap; a signing key pair to exercise KMIP sign/verify where applicable.
- Performance counters: operations/sec, latency p95/p99 for unwrap.

We will also run the rotation/fallback scenario during the window:
- Rotation policy we expect: 90-day DEK rotation by default, with an overlap (alias window) of 7 days where requests are accepted against the old and new DEK; automated fallback if rekey fails for 5 minutes.
- If Cascadia requires a shorter or longer rotation cadence, note it now so we can simulate the exact policy.

Please confirm you can provide the test vectors and the PEM bundle ahead of the test week (two business days prior preferred). I've attached the checklist for your operations team to fill.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
